title: Department Rule on the Late Filing Add-On in Estimated Assessments
content:
**1.** In an estimated assessment on the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, a late filing add-on is added to the uplift, and the uplift and the add-on together, as their sum, are what the estimate applies.

**2.** The add-on follows the late report penalties booked on the account within the estimate history months, 24:

| Late report penalties booked within 24 months | Add-on |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 0.5 |
| Exactly one | 0.25 |
| None | Nothing is added |

**3.** The 24-month window is counted in whole months back from the day the estimate is booked, by the entry dates of the late report penalties in the account's balance history.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- **One penalty in the window.** An account with an uplift of 1.25 and one late report penalty booked 8 months earlier applies 1.25 and 0.25 together, that is 1.5.
- **Two penalties in the window.** The same account with a second late report penalty booked 14 months earlier applies 1.25 and 0.5 together, that is 1.75.
- **Penalty outside the window.** A late report penalty booked 26 months earlier is outside the 24 months; with no other penalty in the window, nothing is added and the uplift stands alone.
